correctness.rationale: All 2n eigenvalues and multiplicities are reconstructed from orthogonal symmetry subspaces. Small branch uses a strict norm lower bound; large branch uses an explicit convex subgradient certificate and exact radical feasibility. Global objective equality follows from averaging without a false assertion of full optimizer uniqueness. Pure-Python independent matrix reconstruction checked 196 spectra, 397 sizes and 21000 feasible parameter competitors; the infinite-family assertion is proved algebraically in RESULT.md, not from enumeration.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary literature establishes the general symmetric-stochastic semidefinite formulation and explicit intact-biclique case, but not the evaluated two-edge-orbit optimum for a single missing crossing edge. The full-text comparison of the bipartite and multipartite examples found no theorem implying the n=8 transition or radical formula. An unrelated fixed-row-mass intact-biclique problem has different feasible supports. A bounded semantic literature search found no exact coverage, but unindexed equivalence remains a material publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible literature may already evaluate the same one-edge-defective K_{n,n} mixing design or an equivalent reduced SDP.
Full global optimizer uniqueness is intentionally not asserted; uniqueness is established only within the automorphism-invariant family.

value.rationale: A single failed crossing edge is the smallest natural graph defect in dense balanced two-community mixing. The complete exact FMMC design reveals a previously unprovided n=8 spectral-activity transition, explicit usable stochastic weights, and exact convergence-rate penalty relative to the intact biclique. This classification is not a textbook deduction from the known one-orbit K_{n,n} expression.
